bullets.text: ML is a subfield of AI, building systems that learn from data without explicit programming.
Core idea: systems learn patterns and make decisions with minimal human intervention.
Used in image recognition, NLP, predictive analytics, and autonomous vehicles.
Growth driven by large datasets, improved computational power, and advanced algorithms.
Broadly classified into Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning.
Supervised Learning: trained on labeled data to predict known outputs (e.g., Regression, Classification).
Unsupervised Learning: finds hidden patterns in unlabeled data (e.g., Clustering, Dimensionality Reduction).
Reinforcement Learning: agent learns by interacting with its environment to maximize rewards.
Model Training: feeding data to a model to learn patterns and adjust internal parameters.
Features and Labels: input variables (features) and target outputs (labels) in supervised learning.
Training and Testing Sets: data split for model training and performance evaluation.
Overfitting: model learns training data too well, leading to poor performance on new data.
Underfitting: model is too simple and fails to capture important patterns in the data.
Linear Regression: models linear relationships for continuous output prediction.
Logistic Regression: used for classification, predicts probability of class membership.
Decision Trees: non-linear model splitting data based on feature values, easy to interpret.
Random Forest: ensemble method combining multiple decision trees for improved performance.
Support Vector Machines (SVM): finds optimal hyperplane for classification, effective in high dimensions.
Neural Networks: inspired by the human brain, learns complex patterns, used in deep learning.
Healthcare: disease diagnosis, drug discovery, personalized treatment recommendations.
Finance: fraud detection, credit scoring, and algorithmic trading.
Marketing: customer segmentation, personalized recommendations, and targeted advertising.
Autonomous Vehicles: processing sensor data, decision-making, and safe navigation.
Natural Language Processing (NLP): language translation, sentiment analysis, text summarization.
Training and Testing: evaluate model performance using separate datasets.
Metrics for classification: accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score.
Metrics for regression: mean squared error (MSE), R-squared.
Cross-Validation: technique to ensure model generalizes well to unseen data.
Hyperparameter Tuning: optimizing model settings for optimal performance using techniques like grid search.
Data Quality and Quantity: models require large amounts of accurate, consistent data.
Interpretability: complex models are often difficult to understand, problematic in high-stakes applications.
Bias in Data: models can inherit biases from training data, leading to unfair outcomes.
Overfitting and Underfitting: common issues affecting model generalization and performance.
Continuous evolution with immense potential for applications.
Advancements in deep learning, reinforcement learning, and explainable AI (XAI).
Increased computational power and datasets will expand ML's role.
ML will integrate more into daily life across various industries.
Ethical considerations and responsible AI practices will be essential.
